What does the ergodic hypothesis assume about the time spent by a system in regions of phase space with the same energy and how does this relate to the probability of microstates?
gold_answer: the time spent by a system in some region of the phase space of microstates with the same energy is proportional to the volume of this region; i.e., that over long periods of time all accessible microstates are equiprobable
alternate: the time spent by a system in some region of the phase space of microstates with the same energy is inversely proportional to the volume of this region; i.e., that over long periods of time less probable microstates become more likely
